enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule for sections 3–9: Sections 3–9 regulate communication, completion and revocation of proposals and acceptances, require acceptance to be absolute, recognise acceptance by performance in the statutory circumstances, and distinguish express from implied promises.

Definition: These provisions govern how proposals and acceptances are communicated, when they become complete, how they may be revoked, and how promises may arise expressly or by implication.

Ingredients / conditions:
1. Identify the proposal, acceptance and relevant communication.
2. Determine when communication is complete under section 4.
3. Test whether revocation was effective under sections 5–6.
4. Test whether acceptance is absolute and unqualified under section 7.
5. Apply performance-based acceptance under section 8 and express/implied promise rules under section 9.

notes: Verified against the official India Code Indian Contract Act, 1872 record and statutory text for sections 3–9.
Section 3: communication of proposals, acceptance and revocation is by an act or omission intended to communicate or having the effect of communicating it.

Section 4: proposal communication completes on knowledge; acceptance completes against proposer when put into transmission beyond acceptor's power and against acceptor when it reaches proposer; revocation completes against maker on dispatch and against recipient on knowledge.
Section 5: proposal may be revoked before communication of acceptance is complete as against proposer; acceptance may be revoked before communication is complete as against acceptor.
Section 6: revocation occurs by notice, lapse of prescribed/reasonable time, failure of a condition precedent, or death/insanity of proposer known to acceptor before acceptance.
Section 7: acceptance must be absolute and unqualified and expressed in a usual/reasonable manner unless the proposal prescribes a manner.
Section 8: performance of the conditions of a proposal, or acceptance of consideration offered with a proposal, constitutes acceptance in the statutory circumstances.
Section 9: promises are express when proposal/acceptance is made in words and implied when made otherwise than in words.
